title: Close a gap you didn't know you had
description: Walk the Fitgap loop against a real role — and watch a critical gap close with a single question, because it was never a real gap.

steps.title: Gates run first — and they halt
steps.body:
Constraints you will not trade away. A `hard` filter that fails blocks analysis entirely; a `soft` one only raises a flag.

The reason is unrecoverable cost. Analysis spends money and tailoring spends an afternoon. A role you could not accept should consume neither.

steps.title: Add the role you're considering
steps.body:
Paste the posting. Fitgap parses it into structured requirements and evaluates your gates immediately — the gate result comes back on creation, not later.

Each requirement carries a `bar`: _familiarity_ and _proficient_ are different requirements wearing the same keyword.

steps.title: Run the analysis
steps.body:
If a hard filter failed this returns `409 gate_failed` and produces nothing.

You can override with `overrideGate: true` and a reason — but the override is recorded on the Analysis. Breaking your own rule is fine. Forgetting that you broke it is not.

steps.title: Two gaps, two different problems
steps.body:
The **C#** requirement comes back typed `blocker` — genuinely not held. That needs a project, or a decision not to pursue the role.

The **imaging** requirement comes back `unarticulated` and `critical`. Fitgap is not saying you lack it. It is saying your record does not evidence it while your history makes absence unlikely — so instead of a verdict, it returns a question.

steps.title: Answer the question
steps.body:
This is the step the API exists for.

No new work. No project. One sentence that was true the whole time and simply was not written down anywhere.

steps.title: Watch it resolve
steps.body:
`resolved: true`, and a new Inventory entry now exists. The next analysis of _any_ target reads the improved record, so this gap will not appear again.

The `blocker` is still there and still needs evidence. That distinction is the entire point: one of these was a capability problem and one was a documentation problem, and treating them the same way is how people end up studying for things they already know.

code_options.code:
# 1 — Set your gates. These are evaluated on every target BEFORE any analysis runs.
curl -X PUT https://api.fitgap.org/v1/filters \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FITGAP_KEY" \
  -d '{"filters":[
        {"id":"flt_remote","kind":"hard","rule":"Remote, or on-site within 45 minutes of New York, NY."},
        {"id":"flt_band","kind":"hard","rule":"Posting must state a compensation range."}
      ]}'

# 2 — Add the role. Fitgap parses it into requirements, each carrying a `bar`.
curl -X POST https://api.fitgap.org/v1/targets \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FITGAP_KEY" \
  -d '{"title":"Senior Data Migration Engineer",
       "sourceText":"Advanced T-SQL. End-to-end migrations between production systems.
                     Experience with RIS, PACS, EHR or similar healthcare applications.
                     Developing or maintaining C# applications."}'

# 3 — Run the analysis. Returns 409 gate_failed if a hard filter did not pass.
curl -X POST https://api.fitgap.org/v1/targets/tgt_91aF/analyses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FITGAP_KEY"

# 4 — Read the gaps. Two came back, and they are not the same kind of problem.
curl https://api.fitgap.org/v1/analyses/ana_04Bq/gaps \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FITGAP_KEY"

# 5 — Answer the excavation question on the `unarticulated` gap.
curl -X POST https://api.fitgap.org/v1/gaps/gap_5Qw2/excavations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FITGAP_KEY" \
  -d '{"answers":[{"questionId":"qst_01",
        "answer":"Yes - I worked with PACS and DICOM as an HL7 Engineer: Merge and Sectra
                  on the radiology side, Zeiss and Optos in ophthalmic imaging."}]}'

# 6 — The gap is resolved, and Inventory now evidences the capability.
curl https://api.fitgap.org/v1/gaps/gap_5Qw2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FITGAP_KEY"
code_options.name: The whole loop
